analysis.title: China 2027 Outlook: Less Drag, More Uncertainty
key_insights: GS expects China real GDP growth to moderate from 4.6% in 2026 to 4.5% in 2027, consistent with a government target nudged down from '4.5-5.0%' to 'around 4.5%'. The forecast is slightly above Bloomberg consensus of 4.4%.

The benign growth forecast does not rely on significant policy easing or a property turnaround. It rests on smaller drags: the property drag narrows from 1.8pp of GDP in 2026 to 1.3pp in 2027, and fiscal tightening becomes 0.5pp smaller, together about a 1pp lift versus 2026.
The augmented fiscal deficit (AFD) is forecast to fall from 11.4% of GDP in 2025 to 10.0% in 2026 and 9.5% in 2027. With a 0.5 fiscal multiplier, that cuts growth by 0.7pp in 2026 and 0.2pp in 2027.

Domestic demand weakened more than expected in 2026: property contracted again, local officials lack incentives to launch projects under Party disciplinary scrutiny, and fiscal policy tightened through tax enforcement and lower spending. Exports and resilience to the oil supply shock were positive surprises.

GS's import-implied real GDP growth measure shows only 2.4% yoy in the first three quarters of 2026, and real retail sales grew under 2% while real FAI fell about 10% yoy. The changes in property, exports and fiscal impulse imply a slowdown 1.2pp steeper than the official GDP data show.

Real export growth is forecast to slow from 8.5% in 2026 to 6.0% in 2027. Nominal USD goods exports are forecast to slow from 22.9% to 13.7% as chip price inflation peaks in 2026 Q4 and lower oil prices temper prices.

Exports rose 21.3% yoy in USD terms in Jan-Sep 2026. Export prices rose 11% (driven by AI-related products and chip-embedded electronics) and volumes rose 9.5%, supported by EVs, batteries, solar and electrical equipment.

A tougher EU trade stance is a key export risk: the EU takes 14% of China's nominal exports and contributed about 2pp to export volume growth in Jan-Sep. GS's baseline assumes escalation is limited by mutual interests and China's leverage over rare earths.

The current account surplus is forecast to rise from 4.4% of GDP in 2026 to 4.9% in 2027, versus the IMF at 4.0% and Bloomberg consensus at 3.6%. The goods trade surplus widens from 6.0% to 6.3% of GDP, and the broad balance of payments improves from 2.9% to 3.5% of GDP.

The property downturn is in its sixth year, with housing indicators down 60-90% from 2020-21 peaks. The sector's share of GDP fell from about 30% to about 15% in 2025 and is expected to stabilize around 8% from 2030. Top-tier cities such as Shanghai and Shenzhen may see prices recover soon, while lower-tier cities may keep falling for years.

The labor market is expected to stay weak. High-tech expansion supports output but is less labor-intensive, and tighter social insurance enforcement raises labor costs. GS expects only incremental policy such as small service subsidies, a higher minimum wage and lower social security contributions for low-wage workers.

Nominal retail sales of goods grew 1.1% yoy in Q1-Q3 2026 versus 4.5% a year earlier. Trade-in funding fell from RMB300bn to RMB250bn, the NEV purchase tax rose from 0% to 5%, and auto sales fell 14.9%, subtracting 1.4pp from retail sales growth.

Real household consumption growth is forecast to rise from 4.0% in 2026 to 4.2% in 2027, with retail sales growth rising from 1.0% to 2.0%. The NEV purchase tax stays at 5% through 2027 and rises to 10% in early 2028, which may pull purchases into Q4 2027. Services consumption is the best source of growth: services retail sales grew 5.0% yoy in Q1-Q3 2026, about 4pp faster than goods.

The household savings rate rose from 32.7% in Q2 to 33.4% in Q3 (seasonally adjusted), and bank deposits keep growing despite falling deposit rates. GS flags a risk that persistent weakness leads to a structural decline in household consumption growth.

FAI is down 7.2% yoy so far in 2026 after a 3.8% decline in 2025. GS forecasts FAI growth improving from about -6% in 2026 to about -3% in 2027, with property investment still contracting at double-digit rates. 'Six Networks' infrastructure investment rises only 2.7% annualized between the 14th and 15th Five-Year Plans.

China exited deflation in 2026: PPI turned positive in March after 41 months of decline and reached 5.7% yoy in October, driven by oil prices (Iran war) and AI hardware prices. Headline CPI was only 0.7% yoy in October and core CPI 0.8%.

GS forecasts PPI inflation of 0.3% in 2027 (from 2.9% in 2026), possibly negative as early as Q2 2027. Headline CPI is forecast at 0.5% (from 0.8%) and core CPI at 0.6% (from 1.0%), versus Bloomberg consensus and IMF at 1.4-1.5% headline. GS's commodity team expects Brent to average $88/bbl in 2027.

On 31 October the PBOC moved its policy rate from the 7-day to the overnight reverse repo rate (1.25%) and set a 1.0-1.5% corridor, effective 2 November. GS views this as equivalent to a 5-10bp cut in front-end interbank rates. GS expects one 10bp policy rate cut in Q4 2027, after the 21st Party Congress and a Fed cut in December 2027, taking the rate to 1.15%.
TSF stock growth is forecast to slow from 8.3% at end-2025 to 7.2% at end-2026 and 6.2% at end-2027 as government bond quotas shrink and private credit demand stays weak.

Fiscal policy tightened in 2026 despite pledges of a more proactive stance. The 12-month moving average AFD fell from 11.4% of GDP in December 2025 to 9.4% in September 2026, the lowest since October 2015. Recent easing (an extra RMB550bn local bond quota, RMB800bn new policy-based financial instruments) is seen as short-lived and aimed at early 2027 growth before the March Two Sessions.

Local government funding is expected to worsen in 2027: land sales revenue is forecast to fall another 20% after 30% in 2026, debt resolution funding drops from RMB2.8tn a year in 2024-26 to RMB800bn a year in 2027-28, and the LGFV exit deadline is mid-2027. Anti-corruption scrutiny keeps local officials from launching projects.

Risks to the 2027 growth forecast are tilted slightly to the downside: renewed US-China tensions, trade barriers (especially Europe), deeper property contraction, local government financial stress, weak policy implementation. Upside risks are faster exports, stronger AI capex and more aggressive stimulus, though stimulus would likely follow a shock such as an export slump, credit event or social instability.

GS is Overweight China equities into 2027, with its equity strategists expecting mid-to-high teen returns. AI hardware profit growth should decelerate while AI application and internet earnings could bounce from a low base. Heavy positioning in AI hard tech points to choppy liquidity and sentiment in early 2027, so strategists favor alpha-over-beta and diversification within the Chinese AI ecosystem.

GS expects long-end China government bond yields to trend lower in 2027 on subdued demand, weak inflation, slowing credit and lower issuance. A possible 25% corporate income tax on government bond interest could push yields up once as a one-off step.

GS forecasts USD/CNY at 6.60/6.50/6.30 in 3/6/12 months, a path faster than FX forwards, supported by a widening trade surplus, a 66% exporter FX conversion ratio in September and RMB internationalization. The PBOC doubled the FX deposit reserve requirement ratio from 2% to 4%, signaling it wants to curb rapid appreciation. GS sees Beijing favoring about 3-5% CNY appreciation per year.

Hong Kong real GDP growth is forecast to slow from 5.0% in 2026 to 3.1% in 2027 as trade and financial services momentum fades. Q3 2026 growth was 5.2% yoy, IPO fundraising reached HK$388bn in the first nine months, and residential price growth is expected to slow from 15% to 7%. Headline CPI is forecast at 1.7% in 2027.

Key catalysts: APEC (18-19 Nov 2026), Politburo meeting (early to mid-Dec), Central Economic Work Conference (mid-Dec), expiry of the tariff/rare earth pause on 10 Jan 2027, Two Sessions (March 2027) and the 21st Party Congress in autumn 2027.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight China equities into 2027, favoring AI application and internet names over AI hardware with an alpha-over-beta approach
trade_ideas.rationale: Equity strategists expect mid-to-high teen returns, with AI application and internet earnings bouncing off a low base.
trade_ideas.risk: Heavy positioning in AI hard tech could cause choppy liquidity and sentiment in early 2027.

trade_ideas.description: Long long-dated China Central Government Bonds, with long-end yields trending lower in 2027
trade_ideas.rationale: Subdued growth, weak inflation, slowing credit growth and lower CGB issuance support long-dated CGBs.
trade_ideas.risk: A possible 25% corporate income tax on government bond interest could push yields higher once on announcement.

trade_ideas.description: Long CNY against USD, with USD/CNY at 6.60/6.50/6.30 in 3/6/12 months
trade_ideas.rationale: A widening goods trade surplus, strong exporter FX conversion and RMB internationalization support the CNY.
trade_ideas.risk: The PBOC is likely to manage the pace of appreciation, as shown by the FX deposit reserve requirement increase from 2% to 4%.

risk_factors: Renewed US-China tensions, including the expiry of the tariff/rare earth pause on 10 Jan 2027.
Significant trade barriers from other major partners, especially the EU.
A deeper property contraction, especially in lower-tier cities with large inventory overhang.
Financial stress among local governments and LGFVs, with the LGFV exit deadline in mid-2027 and land sales down another 20%.
Weak policy implementation and anti-corruption scrutiny limiting local officials' willingness to launch projects.
Structural decline in household consumption growth after several years of weak domestic demand.
Weak labor market and AI-related job displacement concerns.
The 21st Party Congress in 2027 could bring heightened risk aversion at all levels of government.
Official GDP looks high relative to alternative measures such as import-implied GDP of 2.4% yoy.
A possible bond tax change could push yields higher.
Upside risks: faster exports, stronger AI capex, more aggressive stimulus.
vol_and_positioning: Investor positioning in AI hard tech equities remains heavy, pointing to a choppy liquidity and sentiment backdrop in early 2027.
geopolitical: US-China relations may become less stable in 2027 after four Trump-Xi meetings in 2026 kept tensions in check.
The extended tariff/rare earth control pause agreed at the Trump-Xi meeting in Washington expires on 10 Jan 2027.
A tougher EU trade stance toward China is a key export risk, with the EU accounting for 14% of China's nominal exports.
The 21st Party Congress in autumn 2027 may bring intensified anti-corruption efforts, security-related restrictions and heightened risk aversion among officials.
The Iran war and the oil supply shock raised oil prices in 2026 and lifted China's PPI.
APEC 2026 in Shenzhen (18-19 Nov) and the G20 Summit in Miami (14-15 Dec) are listed as upcoming catalysts.

tension_points.bull_case: Less drag from property (1.8pp to 1.3pp) and fiscal tightening (0.5pp smaller) gives about a 1pp lift versus 2026, supporting 4.5% growth. Real exports stay resilient at 6.0% and consumption edges up to 4.3%.
tension_points.bear_case: Official GDP looks high relative to import-implied growth of 2.4%, retail sales under 2% and FAI down about 10%. Sentiment is extremely weak, the labor market is soft, local government finances are stretched, and the Party Congress may raise risk aversion among officials.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sharp slowdown in export growth, a deeper property contraction, or renewed US-China tensions, for example after the tariff/rare earth pause expires on 10 Jan 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Equity strategists expect mid-to-high teen returns, with AI application and internet earnings bouncing off a low base and driving a valuation recovery.
tension_points.bear_case: AI hardware profit growth decelerates and investor positioning in AI hard tech is still heavy, pointing to choppy liquidity and sentiment in early 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Subdued demand, weak inflation, slowing credit growth and lower CGB issuance push long-end yields lower.
tension_points.bear_case: A possible 25% corporate income tax on interest from central and local government bonds could push yields higher on announcement.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Announcement of the bond interest tax change, which GS sees as a one-off step-up in yields rather than a reversal.

theme_stances.key_argument: Smaller property and fiscal drags, not stimulus, keep real GDP growth near 4.5% in 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: Less drag from the property and fiscal impulse is the key reason

theme_stances.key_argument: A growing goods trade surplus and strong exporter FX conversion should keep supporting the CNY.
theme_stances.evidence: Our baseline appreciation path is faster than implied by FX forwards

theme_stances.key_argument: Below-consensus inflation, subdued growth and slowing credit growth support lower Chinese interest rates.
theme_stances.evidence: This supports our “lower for longer” projection of China’s interest rates
